# Sanctioned apiKeyHelper mentions, keyed by a hash of the clause containing
# them (whitespace-normalised, so reflowing prose does not churn this file but
# rewording does).
#
# WHY AN ALLOWLIST. apiKeyHelper shadows a healthy claude.ai OAuth login on
# claude-code >= 2.1.205 and was retired on 2026-07-10 after a multi-day mesh
# outage (anthropics/claude-code#11587, ce-77ip). Earlier versions of the guard
# tried to judge whether prose recommended or disclaimed the wiring, and were
# defeated four times: by an unseen phrasing, by a disclaimer in a neighbouring
# clause, by a first-occurrence shortcut, and finally by a single clause holding
# both ("apiKeyHelper is retired, but use token-refresher as apiKeyHelper").
# Distinguishing those needs parsing, not pattern matching.
#
# So the guard stops guessing. Every mention must be listed here, which makes
# adding or rewording one a deliberate act a human reviews. Each entry below was
# read and confirmed to describe the wiring as RETIRED, or to narrate its
# history, never to recommend it.
#
# To add an entry: run `go test ./internal/deploy/ -run TestNoAPIKeyHelperInstructions`.
# The failure prints the clause and the exact line to paste. Read the clause
# first — if it recommends the wiring, delete the prose instead of listing it.

# Makefile — install target warns against it; uninstall keeps cleanup guidance.

745dfcca702efe2a  # Makefile: install-token-refresher-launchagent, no apiKeyHelper step
f436665c337f64f7  # Makefile: uninstall still clears the retired apiKeyHelper

48452e1f776ac17e  # README: "That wiring was removed from the host on 2026-07-10..."
dfec5ae9366ca09c  # README: how the helper masked real errors as "exited 2"
